13.question: Which interval is the bullish FVG?
13.context: Candle 1: O98 H100 L97 C99. Candle 2: O99 H105 L98 C104. Candle 3: O104 H107 L102 C106.
13.explanation: H1 is 100 and L3 is 102. The middle body is not the interval.

13.question: What is CE, and how deep is this return?
13.context: Saved bullish FVG 100–102; a later candle reaches 101 but not 100.
options: CE is 101; a midpoint test, not a full traversal
CE is 102; the whole gap is filled
CE is 100; there is no return
CE changes to the return candle’s close
13.explanation: (100 + 102) ÷ 2 = 101. Reaching the midpoint differs from reaching the far edge at 100.

13.question: Does the completed chart contain a bullish FVG?
13.context: Candle 1 high = 100; candle 3 low = 99.5. Candle 2 has a very large bullish body.
options: No; the outer ranges overlap
Yes; the middle body is large
Yes; every bullish departure is an FVG
Only if the next candle rises
13.explanation: The strict H1 < L3 test fails. Candle size and later outcomes cannot change that geometry.

13.question: What should the paper record say?
13.context: A limit entry is 101. Every later low stays at or above 101.5 until expiry; price then rises.
options: Unfilled idea under the stated rules
Winning trade because direction was right
Entry at 101.5 without changing the plan
A guaranteed later fill
13.explanation: The market did not reach 101. A correct directional idea is not an executed trade.

13.question: Is this gap objectively in discount?
13.context: FVG 100–102. One selected range is 90–110; another is 96–116.
options: Its label depends on the stated range anchors
Yes, because bullish gaps are always in discount
No, because 102 is always expensive
The gap width determines discount
13.explanation: The midpoints are 100 and 106. The same prices occupy different halves of the two chosen ranges.

13.question: Can this OHLC candle prove which order executed first?
13.context: After entry at 101, a later candle has H108 and L97. Stop 98; target 107. No finer data is available.
options: No; record an ambiguous sequence or use a stated conservative rule
Yes; always award the target
Yes; the closing price reveals the entire path
Yes; ignore the low after entry
13.explanation: Both prices lie inside the bar. OHLC does not reveal their order; fills also require explicit assumptions.

14.question: Has the bearish closing condition been met?
14.context: Original bullish FVG 100–104. Next candle: O103 H105 L99 C102.
options: No; the low crossed 100 but the close did not
Yes; any wick qualifies a closing rule
Yes; the close must be below 104 only
The box should be redrawn to 99–102
14.explanation: A close-through rule requires C < 100. The wick alone does not satisfy it.

14.question: Which direction is this possible inversion?
14.context: Original bearish FVG 106–110; a completed candle closes at 111. Price later declines to 108.
options: Bullish inversion, approached from above
Bearish inversion, approached from below
A newly drawn gap at 108–111
A guaranteed long entry
14.explanation: The close exceeds the original upper edge. The later return comes from above into the saved zone.

14.question: Which statement keeps the two rules distinct?
14.context: Bullish FVG 100–104. Test candle O102 C99.
options: It closes below 100, but its entire body is not below 100
Its entire body is below 100
It fails the close-below test
The original boundaries change to 99–102
14.explanation: The body spans 99–102. A whole-body-below condition is stricter than a close-below condition.

14.question: When did the qualified retest occur?
14.context: A bullish FVG is touched before any close below it. Later it closes through the lower edge but never returns.
options: There was no post-qualification retest
The earlier touch becomes a retest retroactively
The breach candle is always a profitable retest
Any touch on the chart qualifies
14.explanation: Qualification must precede the retest used by the model. Future events cannot change the earlier information set.

14.question: What happened to the trade and the closing rule?
14.context: Short 101; stop 105. Original zone 100–104. Later candle H105 C103. Failure rule: close above 104.
options: Stop reached; closing-based pattern failure not met
Both the stop and closing failure were avoided
The stop can be ignored because the close is 103
The zone must be moved upward
14.explanation: Intrabar protection and closing-based chart classification are separate. Costs and fill assumptions still apply.

14.question: Does an IFVG label establish positive expectancy?
14.context: A set of screenshots shows only successful opposite-side reactions.
options: No; define rules and include failures, no returns and costs
Yes; the screenshots prove it
Yes; inversion is always stronger than the original gap
Only candle colour matters
14.explanation: Selected winners cannot estimate performance. The formation is descriptive; a strategy needs a complete sample.

15.question: Which reference is the run’s first opening?
15.context: A: O106 C104. B: O104 C102. C: O102 C101. The rule selects all three candles.
options: The next departure close
15.explanation: A begins the selected run. Using C opening at 102 would change the selection.

15.question: Which midpoint pair is correct?
options: Full 103; body 103.5
Full 103.5; body 103
Both 106
Both 101
15.explanation: Each midpoint is the mean of its own boundaries. “Mean threshold” without a stated range is ambiguous.

15.question: Which observation can ordinary OHLC support?
15.context: Price returns to a saved order-block opening and closes above it.
options: The reference was revisited and the candle closed above it
A named bank bought there
All original orders are now filled
The next return must fail
15.explanation: The candle reports prices, not participant identities or remaining inventory.

15.question: Did this return reach mean threshold?
15.context: Full range 99–107, midpoint 103. Price returns from above to 106 and rises.
options: No; it reached the opening reference, not 103
Yes; any touch is a midpoint test
Yes; the midpoint moves to 106
No; the block never existed
15.explanation: Return depth matters. The saved midpoint remains 103 when price turns at 106.

15.question: What is the actual overlap?
options: There is no overlap
15.explanation: The larger lower boundary is 105 and the smaller upper boundary is 107.

15.question: What is the planned reward-to-risk before costs?
options: 2R; risk 7.5 and reward 15
3R; risk 5 and reward 15
Guaranteed profit of 15
15.explanation: 106 − 98.5 = 7.5; 121 − 106 = 15. A planned ratio is not a realized return or expectancy.

16.question: When is the illustrated bearish sequence complete?
16.context: A high110 → B low100 → C high112 → D close98.
options: At D, after the sweep and close below B
At C solely because it exceeds A
At A before any later swings
Only after a profitable trade
16.explanation: C supplies the sweep; D supplies the later structural break required by this example.

16.question: What changed in the failed-swing comparison?
16.context: A high110; B low100; C high108; then D close98.
options: C did not exceed A before the break below B
There was a sweep above 110
B was never broken
The same external-high sweep occurred
16.explanation: 108 is below 110. This is the mitigation-block comparison used in the lesson, not the same swept-high path.

16.question: Which band belongs to both references?
16.explanation: Use max(lower edges) and min(upper edges). The positive-width intersection is 102–104.

16.question: Does this pair have positive-width overlap?
options: No; they only touch at 104
Yes; 104–106 is shared
Yes; 100–106 is shared
Only if the next candle falls
16.explanation: The intersection has zero width. Later direction cannot change the earlier interval geometry.

16.question: Which approach matches the bullish mirror?
16.context: A low100 → B high110 → C low98 → D close112. Saved reference 106–110.
options: A later decline from above into 106–110
A rally from below after a bearish break
A touch before D counted retrospectively
Any candle regardless of time
16.explanation: The upward break qualifies the example before the later return from above.

16.question: Which is the defensible study conclusion?
16.context: Two overlapping labels arise from the same move; the sample contains only attractive retests.
options: The drawings may be related; performance still needs a complete rule-based sample
Two labels prove twice the probability
The Unicorn name guarantees a high win rate
Failures can be removed because they are invalid afterward
16.explanation: Overlapping references need not be independent evidence. Include failed, expired and ambiguous cases.
